thread:
lina: Quick all-hands follow-up thread for pricing/packaging/usage questions. Drop short clarifying Qs and we'll route.
sam: Starting with credits: what's the canonical expiry policy for trial/promo credits? Customers ask if they roll monthly.
julia: Legal/Finance: default is 12 months from issue date, non-transferable and non-refundable unless the promo explicitly states otherwise. We'll add exact clause to the billing TOS.
lina: Thanks @julia. Sam, can you put an item on the docs board to update the public FAQ?
sam: Done. I'll add the draft and ping for review.
maya: Rate-limits: are there separate per-minute burst caps or just per-second soft limits + queuing behavior? Need clear numbers for CSMs.
ethan: Hosted defaults: soft ~10 rps per project (about 600 rpm). We allow a short queue/grace window (default 60s) before 429s. Responses include headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`.
ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout of rate-limit headers in us-west-2 complete.
maya: Perfect. Can we also expose a simple backoff header/guide in the SDKs?
ethan: Yes  SDKs (python/js) will add helpers to parse headers and an exponential backoff utility this sprint.
tim: From sales: Dedicated contracts can include a prepaid burst pool as an add-on (negotiated pricing). That helps customers who need short spikes without moving to Reserved capacity.
maya: How are bursts billed vs committed capacity? Is the burst pool usage metered differently?
julia: Billing: committed units are billed under the reserved contract; burst pool is prepaid in minutes or GPU-hours per contract and consumed from that bucket. We'll add a clear line to the pricing repo.
sam: Can credits be applied to Marketplace add-ons or third-party vendor purchases? Several customers asked.
julia: Default: credits apply to Redwood API usage only. Marketplace purchases are billed separately unless a promo explicitly opts in to cover them. We'll document exceptions.
ethan: Ops question: can grace/queue behavior be configurable per org? Some customers prefer immediate 429s to avoid queued cost spikes.
nina: (note: not a participant)
ops-bot: ticket ORG-881 created for per-org throttle-grace config; assigned to eng-runtime.
lina: Good. DevEx, can you produce a one-pager playbook for CSM/Sales with quick commands and thresholds (cURL examples parsing headers, suggested backoff, when to recommend Dedicated/Optimize)?
devex: Yup. I'll draft a one-pager: sections for "observing limits" (headers + examples), "short-term mitigations" (batching, small retries), and "when to recommend Dedicated/Optimize". Draft by Friday.
maya: Also: will we surface queue ETA/position in headers if requests are queued? That would help customer UX.
ethan: We currently expose reset/remaining but not ETA. It's on the backlog; adding ORG-882 to evaluate queue ETA header (perf analysis needed).
sam: One more finance nuance: do issued credits that expire get reclaimed from invoices retroactively? Customers worry about unexpected chargebacks.
julia: No retroactive reclaiming. If credits expire unused, they simply cannot be applied to future invoices. We'll include example scenarios in the FAQ to reduce confusion.
lina: Action items: 1) @sam update billing FAQ (credits clause) 2) @devex one-pager on rate limits/playbook 3) @eng-runtime review per-org grace ticket (ORG-881) 4) @legal publish Marketplace credits exceptions. I'll compile a short all-hands follow-up doc and post the link in #docs.
tim: Minor ask: can we provide a sample SLA blurb for sales decks that explains burst pools and soft limits? Small paragraph will do.
devex: Adding a "sales blurb" section to the one-pager.
maya: Thanks everyone  this helps. If I hear more customer pushback I'll add specific examples here.
lina: Thanks all. Closing thread; will post doc link when complete.
